docs.title: soft_primaries_numpy(task: JetScapeTask) -> typing.Any
docs.text: The undecayed (primary) hadrons of the first N oversamples this event, as sampled before any decay (iSS N, with soft_set_compact_output): the soft_hadrons_numpy dict, sample_counts with N entries. None if none were kept. Takes them over without copying: call it once per event, after soft_hadrons_numpy.

docs.title: soft_sample_cells(task: JetScapeTask, cells: typing.Annotated[numpy.typing.ArrayLike, numpy.float32], seed: typing.SupportsInt | typing.SupportsIndex, n_samples: typing.SupportsInt | typing.SupportsIndex) -> dict
docs.text: Sample the given surface cells now, outside the framework's event loop: an (N, 32) float32 array (SURFACE_CELL_COLUMNS, e.g. a particlize file's surface unit), this seed and n_samples oversamples. Returns soft_hadrons_numpy's dict (one entry of sample_counts per oversample; none for no cells); with iSS the undecayed hadrons follow from soft_primaries_numpy. Equal to replaying the cells through the event loop with soft_set_next_random_seed. The module must be initialised (Init); it need not be in a task list.

docs.title: soft_set_compact_output(task: JetScapeTask, on: bool = True) -> None
docs.text: From the next event on, hand the hadrons over as flat arrays instead of one Hadron object each: the same soft_hadrons_numpy result with ~8x less memory. soft_hadrons_numpy then takes the arrays over without copying, so call it once per event. The framework's Hadron_list_ stays empty (no bulk hadrons for writers or afterburners). iSS: ExecuteTask only.

docs.title: soft_set_next_random_seed(task: JetScapeTask, seed: typing.SupportsInt | typing.SupportsIndex) -> None
docs.text: Use seed for the next event's sampling (one-shot) instead of a draw from the module's generator.

docs.title: soft_set_number_of_samples(task: JetScapeTask, n: typing.SupportsInt | typing.SupportsIndex) -> None
docs.text: Samples (oversamples) per event from the next event on (iSS: number_of_repeated_sampling). Call after Init().

docs.title: to_awkward(obj, position=False, charge=False, by_unit=False)
docs.text:
The nested awkward view of a HadronArray, a hadron dict or a record table.

position: add the nested position (HadronArray; records always carry theirs). charge: add a charge field [e] from the PDG (needs particle). by_unit: a HadronArray read from a file (from_h5): units x samples x hadrons, over info["unit_offsets"].

docs.title: unregister_module(name: str) -> bool
docs.text: Remove a Python module registered with register_module(); False if the name was not one.

docs.title: xml_add_user_blocks(text: str) -> int
docs.text:
Append the children of <jetscape> in text to the open user XML, in memory.

After JetScape.Init(), so the automatic task list never sees them: modules made afterwards (create_module + Init) read their settings from them, while the event loop keeps exactly the tasks the file had. A block the user XML has already is refused. Returns the number of blocks added.

docs.title: Run events
docs.text: Run X-SCAPE from Python and read each event's results while it is still in memory. The guide is The Pythonic interface; modules of your own are on Writing modules in Python.

docs.title: One event, results in memory
docs.text:
JobDir gives the run a private working directory (MUSIC, 3dMCGlauber and iSS write side files into the current directory) and points the XML's relative paths at the build. per_event runs Init() on entry and Finish() on exit; inside the loop the event's data is still there.

import numpy as np
import jetscape as js

with js.JobDir("out_first", "oo_workflow.xml") as job:          # the O+O example's XML
    with js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml, n_events=1) as driver:
        for i in driver.events():                                # after the event, before clearing
            partons = driver.energy_loss_manager.final_parton_array()   # numpy records
            jet = driver.hadronization_manager.hadron_array()          # HadronArray
            print(f"event {i}: {len(partons)} final partons,",
                  f"leading parton pT {np.hypot(partons['px'], partons['py']).max():.1f} GeV,",
                  f"{len(jet)} jet hadrons")

final_parton_array() has the fields shower, pid, pstat, E, px, py, pz, t, x, y, z, mass, col, acol; hadron_array() holds pid, pstat, p (E, px, py, pz) and x (t, x, y, z) per hadron. The other modules are driver properties too: driver.hydro, driver.soft_particlization (iSS), driver.initial_state.

docs.title: Skip events that fail
docs.text:
A rare module error (Matter's "minus log of sudakov negative") would stop the loop. With on_error the event is reported, cleared and skipped, as the productions do:

skipped = []
for i in driver.events(on_error=lambda i, exc: skipped.append((i, str(exc)))):
    ...

docs.title: Run a whole XML without a Python loop
docs.text:
from jetscape.run_jetscape import run_automatic

run_automatic(main_xml, user_xml)          # modules from the XML, the C++ event loop

docs.title: A module in Python
docs.text:
Subclass the C++ base class and register it; an XML can then name it, and xml_parameters become XML parameters (from Writing modules in Python):

import jetscape as js
from jetscape import pyjetscape_core as core

@js.module("CustomModuleToySplitV2", section="Eloss")
class ToySplitV2(core.JetEnergyLoss):
    """A parton above e_min splits into two halves at t >= t_split."""

    xml_parameters = {"t_split": 1.0, "e_min": 30.0}

    def DoEnergyLoss(self, deltaT, time, Q2, pIn, pOut):
        p = pIn[0]
        if time >= self.t_split and p.e() > self.e_min:
            E, px, py, pz = p.momentum
            return [js.make_parton(p.pid(), (E / 2, px / 2, s * 1.0, pz / 2),
                                   position=p.position) for s in (+1, -1)]

docs.title: jetscape.pythonic
docs.text:
python/jetscape/pythonic.py

The Pythonic layer over the bound classes (docs/Plans/PLAN_pyjetscape_pythonic.md). Additive: install() puts new methods and properties onto the classes of pyjetscape_core and refuses any name a class already has, so no bound method can be shadowed and every existing script keeps working. jetscape/init calls install() once; importing jetscape.pyjetscape_core directly runs jetscape/init first, so the layer is always there.

Naming: a method ending in _array() returns numpy data, filled once per event; a plain noun (showers, nodes, final_partons()) returns objects. Momentum (E, px, py, pz), position (t, x, y, z): the order of FourVector.comp(i).

Properties on the bound classes are non-data descriptors (_Prop): an instance attribute of the same name, as a Python module may set (self.rng = ...), still wins.

docs.text: A Parton by keywords: momentum (E, px, py, pz) and position (t, x, y, z) as any 4-sequence or a FourVector; colour tags optional. cls=Photon for a photon.

docs.text: A Hadron by keywords: momentum (E, px, py, pz), position (t, x, y, z) as any 4-sequence or a FourVector; without a mass the PDG mass is used (C++ Hadron).

docs.title: module(name: str, section: str = '') -> 'Callable[[type], type]'
docs.text: Class decorator: register a Python module under name (register_module), with a main-XML default built from the class's xml_parameters ({key: default}, int, float, str or bool). The class's InitTask first sets self. from [section, name, key] in the XML; the defaults are also class attributes, so a module built by hand has them before Init. Use a CustomModule... name for modules the XML names ().

docs.title: per_event(main_xml: str | None = None, user_xml: str | None = None, tasks: Sequence | None = None, n_events: int | None = None) -> 'core.JetScapePerEvent'
docs.text:
A JetScapePerEvent driver by keywords: the XML files, a by-hand pipeline (tasks added in order; else the XML's task list) and the number of events.

with js.per_event(main_xml, user_xml) as driver:
    for _ in driver.events():
        fp = driver.energy_loss_manager.final_parton_array()

The bound constructor JetScapePerEvent() stays as it is.

docs.title: jetscape.run_jetscape
docs.text:
python/jetscape/run_jetscape.py

High-level simulation driver helpers.

Two modes are supported — matching the two values of in the JETSCAPE XML:

Mode A — automatic task list (enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination = true) run_automatic(main_xml, user_xml) All modules are instantiated from the XML by the C++ factory. No Python module injection is possible in this mode.

Mode B — manual task list (enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination = false) run_manual(main_xml, user_xml, modules) Modules are supplied explicitly as a Python list. Python trampoline modules (e.g. PyFNOHydro) are supported. The helper validates that the supplied list is in a legal pipeline order before calling js.Add().

Mode C — per-event external loop (either XML configuration) per_event_loop(main_xml, user_xml, ...) # generator, yields once per event run_per_event(main_xml, user_xml, on_event, ...) # callback per event Uses JetScapePerEvent so the event loop runs in Python. The per-event module results are accessible (e.g. via JetScapeSignalManager) after the event executes and before its memory is released. Works with the automatic (modules=None) or manual (modules=[...]) task list.

Usage example (Mode C): from jetscape import JetScapeSignalManager from jetscape.run_jetscape import per_event_loop

for js in per_event_loop("config/jetscape_main.xml",
                         "config/jetscape_user.xml"):
    hydro = JetScapeSignalManager.Instance().GetHydroPointer()
    if hydro is not None:
        info = hydro.get_bulk_info()

Usage example (Mode A): from python.jetscape.run_jetscape import run_automatic js = run_automatic("config/jetscape_main.xml", "config/jetscape_user_MUSIC.xml")

Usage example (Mode B): from python.jetscape import create_module from python.jetscape.fno_hydro import PyFNOHydro from python.jetscape.run_jetscape import run_manual

ini      = create_module("TrentoInitial")
preeq    = create_module("FreestreamMilne")
fno      = PyFNOHydro("models/traced.pt", config)
# JetEnergyLossManager / JetEnergyLoss are not in the module factory: for jet
# energy loss construct pyjetscape_core.JetEnergyLossManager() and JetEnergyLoss()
# directly and Add() a create_module("Matter") to them.

js = run_manual(
    "config/jetscape_main.xml",
    "jetscape_user_fno.xml",           # a user XML with a <Hydro><FNO> block
    [ini, preeq, fno],
)   # runs Init(), Exec() and Finish()

docs.title: run_automatic(main_xml: str, user_xml: str) -> JetScape
docs.text:
Run a fully XML-driven JETSCAPE pipeline.

The XML must contain::

<enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination>true</enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination>

All modules are instantiated from the XML by the C++ factory. No Python module injection is possible in this mode.

Parameters:

  • main_xml (str) –

    Path to the main (default parameters) XML file.

  • user_xml (str) –

    Path to the user (overrides) XML file.

Returns:

  • JetScape –

    The framework object after Finish() has been called.

docs.title: run_manual(main_xml: str, user_xml: str, modules: Sequence, n_events: int | None = None) -> JetScape
docs.text:
Run a JETSCAPE pipeline with an explicit module list.

The XML must contain::

<enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination>false</enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination>

Modules are added in the order supplied. Python trampoline modules (e.g. PyFNOHydro) are supported alongside C++ modules obtained via create_module().

The helper validates that the supplied top-level modules are in a legal pipeline stage order before handing them to JetScape.Add().

Parameters:

  • main_xml (str) –

    Path to the main (default parameters) XML file.

  • user_xml (str) –

    Path to the user (overrides) XML file.

  • modules (sequence of JetScapeTask) –

    Top-level modules added to JetScape in pipeline order, e.g.::

    [ini, preeq, fno, jloss_manager, hadro_manager]

    Note: sub-modules (JetEnergyLoss, Hadronization, etc.) must already be nested inside their managers via manager.Add() before calling run_manual().

  • n_events (int, default: None ) –

    Override the number of events from the XML.

Returns:

  • JetScape –

    The framework object after Finish() has been called.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the module list is in an illegal pipeline order.

docs.title: per_event_loop(main_xml: str, user_xml: str, modules: Sequence | None = None, n_events: int | None = None, start_event: int = 0) -> Iterator[JetScapePerEvent]
docs.text:
Iterate over a JETSCAPE run one event at a time.

Yields the JetScapePerEvent driver once per event, after the event has been executed but before its memory is released, so the caller can read the live module results for that event::

from jetscape import JetScapeSignalManager
from jetscape.run_jetscape import per_event_loop

for js in per_event_loop(main_xml, user_xml):
    hydro = JetScapeSignalManager.Instance().GetHydroPointer()
    if hydro is not None:
        info = hydro.get_bulk_info()
    # ... analyse this event ...
# Finish() is called automatically when the loop ends.

The memory for each event is released (ClearPerEvent) immediately after the consumer resumes the generator, and Finish() is called when iteration ends or the generator is closed (e.g. on an early break).

Parameters:

  • main_xml (str) –

    Path to the main (default parameters) XML file.

  • user_xml (str) –

    Path to the user (overrides) XML file.

  • modules (sequence of JetScapeTask, default: None ) –

    Manual (Mode B) pipeline. If omitted, the task list is taken from the XML (Mode A). When given, the same pipeline-order validation as run_manual() is applied.

  • n_events (int, default: None ) –

    Override the number of events from the XML.

  • start_event (int, default: 0 ) –

    Starting event number for the global event counter.

Yields:

  • JetScapePerEvent –

    The driver object, with the current event's data available in memory.

docs.title: run_per_event(main_xml: str, user_xml: str, on_event: Callable[[JetScapePerEvent], None], modules: Sequence | None = None, n_events: int | None = None, start_event: int = 0) -> JetScapePerEvent
docs.text:
Run a JETSCAPE simulation, invoking a callback once per event.

Callback-based counterpart to per_event_loop(). on_event(js) is called for each event after ExecPerEvent() and before ClearPerEvent(), i.e. while the event's module results are still in memory::

def analyse(js):
    hydro = JetScapeSignalManager.Instance().GetHydroPointer()
    ...

run_per_event(main_xml, user_xml, analyse)

Parameters:

  • main_xml (str) –

    XML configuration file paths.

  • user_xml (str) –

    XML configuration file paths.

  • on_event (callable) –

    Called as on_event(js) for each event, with the live data in memory.

  • modules (sequence of JetScapeTask, default: None ) –

    Manual (Mode B) pipeline; if omitted the XML task list (Mode A) is used.

  • n_events (int, default: None ) –

    Override the number of events from the XML.

  • start_event (int, default: 0 ) –

    Starting event number for the global event counter.

Returns:

  • JetScapePerEvent –

    The driver object after Finish() has been called.

docs.title: jetscape.workdir
docs.text:
python/jetscape/workdir.py

A job's private working directory and its seed, for the production scripts and for scripts and notebooks of one's own (docs/Plans/PLAN_container_user.md, step 1). Pure Python, no build needed to import.

The functions moved here unchanged from example/prod_AuAu_0_10/run_prod.py, which re-exports them under the same names, so every production script keeps calling rp.enter_workdir(a, ...) etc. They take the scripts' parsed arguments a (any object with the attributes they read: build, main_xml, workdir, in_build, keep_workdir, seed, ...).

For a script of one's own, JobDir does the same with plain arguments:

import jetscape as js
from jetscape.workdir import JobDir

with JobDir("out", "my_job.xml") as job:            # -> out/my_job.xml, out/work/my_job
    with js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml) as driver:
        for i in driver.events():
            ...

docs.title: XMLProblem(problems)
docs.text:
Bases: FileNotFoundError

The job's XMLs can't run with this X-SCAPE: a user XML tag the main XML lacks, or an input of the run with no file behind it. Raised before anything runs. problems lists them; the message says what to do.

docs.title: JobDir(out_dir, user_xml, *, name=None, main_xml=None, build=None, keep=False)
docs.text:
A job's private working directory, as the production scripts make it, for a script or notebook of one's own -- runnable from any writable directory (a container's /work).

On entering: user_xml is copied to <out_dir>/<name>.xml (job.user_xml), the main XML to <out_dir>/work/<name>/jetscape_main.xml (job.main_xml), their '../' paths made absolute against the build, music_input copied and the build's tables linked (enter_workdir), and the current directory changed to job.path, where the modules write their side files (3dMCGlauber's events_summary.dat, ...).

On leaving: back to the directory it was entered from; job.path is removed unless keep or an exception left the block (then it is kept and printed).

build: default jetscape.paths.build_dir() ($JETSCAPE_BUILD, else /build_gpu); main_xml: default jetscape.paths.main_xml(); name: default the user XML's stem.

docs.title: add_seed_args(p: argparse.ArgumentParser, drives: str) -> None
docs.text: --seed, --campaign, --index and --seed-registry (run_prod.py and run_prod_jet.py).

docs.title: output_name(a, base: str) -> str
docs.text: The output file name: --out, else by seed when the seed is given -- []seed.h5 -- and by job number when it is drawn (--seed 0, with the start time as the campaign if none was given): .h5.

docs.title: resolve_seed(a, out_h5: str, record: bool = True) -> None
docs.text:
Make a.seed concrete and note where it came from (a.seed_source).

--seed 0 draws from OS entropy (secrets) a seed in 1..SEED_MAX that the registry does not hold yet. With record the seed is appended to the registry (under an exclusive lock, so jobs starting together cannot draw the same one); an explicit seed is recorded too, and reported when the registry has it for another file (the same collisions: fine for paired comparisons, not for more statistics).

docs.title: resolve_parent_path(text: str, build: str) -> tuple
docs.text:
A '../' path of an XML -> (absolute path, whether it exists).

The path relative to build (the working directory of an in-build run); if that's missing, build joined with each tail of its parts, longest first. An installed tree (the xscape wheel's share/xscape) has no ../external_packages or ../config, and keeps iSS_tables, iSS_parameters.dat and config/ directly in it. So ../external_packages/iSS/iSS_tables resolves to /iSS_tables and ../config/HH_LightExcitedMesons.xml to /config/HH_LightExcitedMesons.xml. The same rule as X-SCAPE's examples/run_xml.py, which run_in_workdir.sh uses.

docs.title: xml_problems(main_xml: str, user_xml: str, build: str) -> list
docs.text: What would stop the job: user XML tags the main XML lacks (X-SCAPE exits the process at the first one, Python included), and the run's '../' inputs with no file behind them, in the build or by their trailing parts in it. Nothing is written. The inputs are not checked when the XML turns automatic module setup off.

docs.title: enter_workdir(a, workdir: str, job_xml_path: str) -> str
docs.text:
Make workdir this job's working directory -> the main XML to use.

The Python counterpart of X-SCAPE's examples/run_in_workdir.sh (which execs the runJetscape binary, so it cannot drive PyJetscape). In the build tree, concurrent jobs share music_input -- MusicWrapper truncates and rewrites it at every MUSIC init, and a job reading it in that window spins forever in MUSIC's StringFind4 -- as well as every file the modules write to the working directory (3dMCGlauber strings_event_.dat and events_summary.dat, MUSIC's momentum_anisotropy / eccentricities / meanpT files, ...). Here each job has its own directory with a private music_input, and the read-only assets come from the build tree:

  • XSCAPE_DATA_DIR -> mcglauber.input (MCGlauberWrapper), LBT-tables fallback
  • HYDROPROGRAMPATH -> MUSIC's EOS tables
  • LBT_TABLES_PATH -> LBT tables
  • symlinks for the dirs still opened relative to the working directory (WORKDIR_LINKS)
  • '../' paths in the main and job XML made absolute (see _absolute_parent_paths)

Before any of it, the XMLs are checked (xml_problems): XMLProblem, a FileNotFoundError, names the user XML tags the main XML lacks and the inputs with no file behind them.

docs.title: job_workdir(a, out_h5: str) -> str
docs.text: This job's working directory: --workdir, else OUTDIR/work/.

docs.title: leave_workdir(a, workdir: str, ok: bool) -> None
docs.text: Remove the working directory after a successful job unless --keep-workdir.

docs.title: pythia_data_problem()
docs.text:
None if pyjetscape_core can be imported, else the reason.

Pythia finds its xmldoc through PYTHIA8DATA or the path compiled into libpythia8. Homebrew's Pythia (macOS) has a working compiled-in path; a relocated conda Pythia (the js_fno env) may not, and then the import aborts the process -- so it is probed in a subprocess, and only when PYTHIA8DATA is unset.

docs.title: hydro_label(build: str) -> str
docs.text:
The production files' hydro attribute: "MUSIC (music4gpu)" or "MUSIC".

From the compiled core's MUSIC_BACKEND (the MUSIC it was linked against: "music", "music4gpu-cuda", "music4gpu-metal"); a core without it (built before) falls back to the old test, "gpu" in the build folder's name (build_gpu).

docs.title: build_or_job_dir(out_dir, user_xml, main_xml=None, *, name=None, keep=False)
docs.text:
Where an example script runs X-SCAPE -> an object with main_xml, user_xml, path.

In a build tree (music_input in the current directory: the old way, cd X-SCAPE/build_gpu and run the script from there) it runs right here with the XMLs as given, as these scripts always did. Anywhere else -- a copy of the examples (xscape-examples), the container's /work, the macOS wheel -- it runs in a JobDir under out_dir (keep: leave its working directory, e.g. for files the XML writes there). Give output paths absolute: a JobDir changes the current directory.

docs.title: jetscape.paths
docs.text:
python/jetscape/paths.py

Where the X-SCAPE tree, its build and the main XML are, for scripts and notebooks that live anywhere -- a copy in a container's /work, a user's own directory -- instead of inside the tree (docs/Plans/PLAN_container_user.md, step 1). Pure Python, no build needed. Paths are absolute but not resolved (symlinks kept), as the production scripts make them.

XSCAPE          the X-SCAPE tree (the production image sets it to /opt/X-SCAPE);
                default: the checkout this package sits in (X-SCAPE/external_packages/
                js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/python/jetscape), else the installed
                tree of the xscape wheel (macOS: site-packages/xscape/share/xscape)
JETSCAPE_BUILD  the build tree to run; default: <XSCAPE>/build_gpu, or the installed
                tree itself, which holds music_input, EOS and the tables

The installed tree of the wheel (cmake --install of X-SCAPE) has config/ and the data of a build tree side by side, so it serves as both XSCAPE and the build.

docs.text: The X-SCAPE tree: $XSCAPE, else the checkout this package sits in, else the xscape wheel's installed tree.

docs.title: build_dir() -> Path
docs.text: The build tree: $JETSCAPE_BUILD, else /build_gpu, else -- an installed tree, which has music_input but no build_gpu -- the X-SCAPE tree itself.

docs.title: main_xml() -> Path
docs.text: X-SCAPE's config/jetscape_main.xml.

docs.title: jetscape.copy_examples
docs.text:
python/jetscape/copy_examples.py

xscape-examples [DEST] -- copy PyJetscape's examples into a writable directory: the console script of the installed package (the xscape wheel), the Python twin of the production image's utils/container/xscape-examples.

xscape-utils [DEST] -- the same for js-contrib's utils/ (jobmon.py, prodwizard.py, h5_inspect.py, remote_transfer/, ...), to read or adapt; jetscape.paths.utils_dir().

The examples write next to themselves, and an installed or image tree is read-only, so they run from a copy:

xscape-examples                 # -> /work/examples in the image, else ./examples
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples

Copies jetscape.paths.examples_dir() (production scripts, notebooks, user XMLs, configs), without outputs (out/, out_*/, *.h5, *.root) and caches; in a git checkout, the tracked files only. Never overwrites: DEST must be new or empty. The copies find the X-SCAPE tree and its build through jetscape.paths ($XSCAPE, $JETSCAPE_BUILD, else the checkout or the installed tree).

docs.title: Write the files
docs.text: Store the hadrons of your own runs in the production's file format, and the writers behind the production files. Which file holds what is on What a production writes.

docs.title: Hadrons of your own run
docs.text:
HadronH5Writer writes one unit per event; the files it makes are read with everything on Analyse the files. Give it an absolute path: JobDir changes the directory.

import os
import jetscape as js
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronH5Writer
from jetscape.records import initiator_rows

out = os.path.abspath("my_hadrons_jet_frag.h5")     # absolute: JobDir changes directory
with js.JobDir("out", "oo_workflow.xml") as job, \
     js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml, n_events=2) as driver, \
     HadronH5Writer(out, tag="jet_frag", n_samples=1, initiators=True) as w:
    had, mgr = driver.hadronization_manager, driver.energy_loss_manager
    n = 0
    for i in driver.events():
        w.append_unit(had.hadron_array().to_dict(), unit=n, event=i,
                      initiators=initiator_rows(mgr.initiator_array()),
                      seed=had.last_random_seed)
        n += 1
  • The bulk hadrons of iSS go into a second writer with tag="bulk_bg" and n_samples= the number of oversamples: call driver.soft_particlization.use_compact_output() before the loop and append driver.soft_particlization.hadron_array().to_dict() per event. The complete version is pythonic/oo_workflow.py in the examples.
  • Extra keywords of append_unit (seed=, pthat=, n_cells=, ...) are stored per unit, in the file's units/ table.

docs.title: What the productions write
docs.text:
The drivers use the other writers on this page themselves:

file written by class <stem>_particlize.h5 run_prod_jet.py --write-particlize ParticlizeH5Writer <stem>_hadrons_<tag>.h5 hadronize.py (per unit: Hadronizer) HadronH5Writer <stem>.h5, the hydro pair run_prod_jet.py PairH5Writer

SurfaceReplay is a hydro module that hands a stored freeze-out surface to iSS inside a JETSCAPE run, so iSS samples it as it would the live hydro's. liquefier_io reads the jet's droplets out of the liquefier during a run.

docs.title: jetscape.hadrons_h5.HadronH5Writer(path, *, tag, n_samples, attrs=None, compression=DEFAULT_COMPRESSION, force=True, keep_bits=None, initiators=False, eta_max=None, charged_only=False, positions=True, hadronization_input=False, partons=False, x_had='none', hadron_scatter=False)
docs.text:
Append units of samples of hadrons (see the module docstring).

keep_bits (default None: lossless) rounds p and x before they are written: an int for both, or a mapping such as {"p": 12, "x": 8}. The precision is recorded on each dataset (hadron_precision).

initiators=True (bulk_jet and jet_frag only) adds the initiators/ group: every append_unit then takes that event's shower initiators, a (K, 11) array in INITIATOR_COLUMNS order (None: none).

eta_max (default None: all hadrons) keeps only hadrons with |eta| < eta_max (pseudorapidity of the stored, i.e. rounded, momenta); charged_only only the charged ones (|pid| in CHARGED); the samples stay, with fewer hadrons. positions=False writes no x (x given to append_unit is ignored). Recorded as the eta_max, charged_only and positions attributes (hadron_selection).

hadronization_input=True (jet_frag only) adds the hadronization_input/ group: every append_unit then takes the event's Pythia input, a dict of pid, col, acol, p (K, 4) [E, px, py, pz] and mass (core.hadronization_input_numpy) or a (K, 8) array in HADRONIZATION_INPUT_COLUMNS order.

partons=True (jet_frag only) adds the partons/ group: every append_unit then takes the event's final partons, a (K, 14) array in PARTON_COLUMNS order, so the jets can be hadronized again from this file alone (run_prod_jet.py --hadrons-only). x_had is recorded on the group: "none" for the partons' production points only.

extra_frag files (the extra hard scatterings) also take scatterings (the event's (S, 8) SCATTER_COLUMNS rows, group scatterings/) and initiator_scatter (each initiator's scattering, initiators/scatter) in append_unit, and with hadron_scatter=True each hadron's scattering (a scatter array in every sample, hadrons/scatter).

docs.title: append_unit(samples, initiators=None, hadronization_input=None, partons=None, scatterings=None, initiator_scatter=None, **unit_scalars)
docs.text: Append one unit. samples is a list of hadron dicts (one per sample, keys pid, pstat, p, x), or one dict with sample_counts (as soft_hadrons_numpy returns); initiators the event's (K, 11) initiator rows, for a writer made with initiators=True; hadronization_input the event's Pythia input, for a writer made with hadronization_input=True; partons the event's final partons, for a writer made with partons=True. Returns the unit index.

docs.text:
Write each event's surfaces and final partons (see the module docstring).

Parameters:

  • out_file_name (str, default: 'particlize.h5' ) –

    Output path.

  • legs (iterable of {"jet", "bg"}, default: ('jet', 'bg') ) –

    Which legs' surfaces to store. Their MUSIC instances must build the surface (<freeze_out_surface>1) and hand it over (skip_surface off, e.g. PairH5Writer(keep_surface=legs)).

  • store_partons (bool, default: True ) –

    Write partons/ and initiators/ (both from the energy-loss manager).

  • bg_id (str, default: 'MUSIC_1' ) –

    Module ids of the two MUSIC instances.

  • jet_id (str, default: 'MUSIC_1' ) –

    Module ids of the two MUSIC instances.

  • compression (str or None, default: DEFAULT ) –

    jetscape.h5_compression spec for the surfaces (default Blosc-zstd: the charge and chemical-potential columns are zero here and cost almost nothing). Partons are gzip'ed (small).

  • music_input (str, default: None ) –

    Text of the job's music_input (iSS reads its EoS id and flags from it). By default ./music_input is read at attach (the job's working directory).

  • T_fo (float, default: None ) –

    MUSIC's freeze-out temperature, recorded.

  • pair_file (str, default: None ) –

    The FNO4d pair file written alongside, recorded (basename).

  • extra_attrs (mapping, default: None ) –

    More root attributes (run provenance), written verbatim.

  • force (bool, default: True ) –

    Overwrite an existing file.

  • sink (callable, default: None ) –

    No file: each event's record goes to sink(record) (see the module docstring).

  • extra_hard (bool, default: False ) –

    The events have other hard scatterings (PythiaGun's ): store scatterings/ and initiators/scatter (Exec's scatterings and shower_scatter).

docs.title: attach(jetscape=None, *, bg=None, jet=None, manager=None)
docs.text:
Find the MUSIC legs and the energy-loss manager; open the file.

Call after JetScape.Init() (and after PairH5Writer.attach, which sets the legs' skip_surface flags). A stored leg found with skip_surface on is switched off here, with a warning.

docs.title: Exec(i=None, *, bg_id=None, bg_key=None, scatterings=None, shower_scatter=None, **diag)
docs.text:
Store this event. Returns its index.

i is the event's index in the pair file (default: the running count; the two must agree -- events skipped by the pair writer must be skipped here too). bg_id names the background: the first event that used it (the pair writer's diag/bg_id). A new value stores the background surface; a repeated one (an event reusing its background) only records the reference. Without a pair writer pass bg_id=i. Extra keywords go to events/. With extra_hard: scatterings the event's (S, 8) rows (SCATTER_COLUMNS) and shower_scatter the hard scattering of each shower (indexed by the shower index; extra_hard_info's parton_scatter).

docs.title: write_events(i, **scalars)
docs.text: Add per-event scalars after Exec (e.g. seeds, wall time).

docs.title: Finish(complete=None)
docs.text: Close the file. Idempotent.

docs.title: jetscape.particlize_h5.add_initiators_from_pair(path, pair=None, *, force=False)
docs.text:
Copy the pair file's shower/initiators into the particlize file path, so it no longer needs the pair file. pair defaults to the file's pair_file, next to it.

Returns True if added, False if the file already had initiators/ (kept unless force). Raises if the pair file is missing, holds no initiators, or has another number of events.

docs.title: jetscape.hadronizer
docs.text:
python/jetscape/hadronizer.py

Hadronizer -- the per-unit work of hadronizing a two-stage hydro event: iSS on a leg's freeze-out cells, ColorlessHadronization on the event's final partons, their seeds, and the hadron files (jetscape.hadrons_h5). One code path for the two places it runs:

example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/hadronize.py      afterwards, from a particlize file
example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_prod_jet.py --hadrons-only
                                             in the production job, from the particlize
                                             writer's memory sink

so the job's hadrons are, by construction, what hadronize.py makes of the same cells, partons and seeds (docs/Plans/PLAN_AuAu_hadrons_only.md).

h = Hadronizer(core, iss=iss, colorless=colorless, base_seed=1, prod=production_key)
h.open("bulk_jet", path, n_samples=1, attrs=common, primary_path=ppath)
h.bulk("bulk_jet", e, cells, h.bulk_jet_seed(e, bg_unit), n_samples=1, event=e,
       initiators=ini)
h.fragments(e, partons, [h.seed("jet_frag", e, s) for s in range(n_frag)],
            initiators=ini)
h.extra_fragments(e, extra_partons, n_frag, initiators=extra_ini,
                  initiator_scatter=scat, scatterings=rows)   # extra hard scatterings
h.close(complete=True)

With extra hard scatterings (PythiaGun's , docs/Plans/PLAN_multi_hard.md) an event's final partons are split by their shower's scattering (jetscape.particlize_h5.split_by_scatter): the trigger's go to jet_frag exactly as without extras (same partons, same seeds), the extras' to extra_frag, with seeds of their own tag: all together in one Colorless call (mode groups) or one call per scattering (per_scattering, each hadron's scattering kept).

iSS runs on given cells through core.soft_sample_cells (X-SCAPE's SoftParticlization::SampleCells): no framework event, so it also works inside a production process whose own event loop must not run again. The iSS and Colorless modules only need Init() (after the JETSCAPE instance's Init has read the XML).

docs.title: jetscape.pair_h5
docs.text:
python/jetscape/pair_h5.py

PairH5Writer -- write an X-SCAPE two-stage MUSIC run as one FNO4d-schema HDF5 file in FastHydro's pair layout: the jet leg (with the CausalLiquefier deposition) as arr, the background leg as arr_bg, the droplets MUSIC was given as source/droplets, and the parton showers as shower/.

IS -> Hard -> NullPreDynamics -> MUSIC_1 (background)
   -> JetEnergyLossManager (Matter + LBT, CausalLiquefier)
   -> MUSIC_2 (same IC + the liquefier source)          -> PairH5Writer
Where each leg is read from
  • Background (MUSIC_1) from the framework copy, bulk_info. Matter and LBT query the first hydro through bulk_info, so it must be filled, and filling it releases MUSIC's native store (MusicWrapper.cc PassHydroEvolutionHistoryToFramework). The copy is cell for cell the native store: both go through get_fluid_cell_with_index and a float copy, so nothing is lost.
  • Jet leg (MUSIC_2) from its native store, which attach() keeps with set_dump_hydro_only(True) on that instance only. Every MUSIC instance reads the first <Hydro><MUSIC> XML block, so this cannot be set per leg in the XML.

Both legs then go through the same jetscape.bulk_sources.resample onto one output grid, so arr - arr_bg is the jet's effect and nothing else: before the first droplet deposits the two legs are bit-identical, which diag/frames_identical records per event.

Layout (on top of jetscape.fno_h5_writer.FnoH5Writer)
  • arr / arr_bg with ntau_freezeout[_bg], tau_freezeout[_bg]. The tau axis grows to the longer leg (the jet leg usually outlives the background); the shorter one is exactly zero after its own freeze-out. arr_bg.shape == arr.shape always.
  • With a reused background (bg_layout="shared", the default for reuse > 1) each background is stored once: in arr_bg_store, in the row of the first event that used it (the other rows are never written and take no space), with arr_bg_rows giving every event's row. arr_bg is then a virtual dataset over the store (a row view, jetscape.fno_h5_writer.write_row_view): it reads exactly like the full layout, event by event, and root attribute bg_layout is "shared". Without reuse the file is written as before (no bg_layout attribute).
  • A reused background is recognised by a fingerprint of its raw frames and then neither read nor resampled again: its frame hashes and edge maxima are those of the event that first used it (verify_bg_reuse checks this). Only bg_layout="full" with a file still reads it every event, to store it in every row.
  • source/droplets (M, 8) + source/offsets, columns droplet_columns. There is no source/S: MUSIC evaluates the liquefier kernel per cell and step and never keeps a gridded source, and a re-deposit on the output grid would not be what MUSIC applied. has_source is therefore false. With an X-SCAPE whose droplets carry the background fluid where they were made, also source/fluid (M, 4), columns fluid_columns (vx, vy, vz, e: lab velocity, energy density; e < 0: not looked up), which <CausalLiquefier><frame>fluid</frame> uses; older files have no source/fluid.
  • shower/ exactly as FastHydro writes it (jetscape.showers).
  • diag/: droplet counts and energies (and how much deposits after the jet leg froze out, which MUSIC never applies), shower counts, MUSIC tau0, per-leg frame counts, bg_id (the first event that used this background -- repeats under setReuseHydro), frames_identical, and per leg the largest energy density on the faces of the output grid ({bg,jet}_edge_e_max on the x and y faces, ..._eta on the eta faces) with, given edge_e_threshold, the flag {bg,jet}_hit_edge.
  • Provenance attributes as in FastHydro's PairedH5Writer (pairing, arr_is, arr_bg_is, source_model, liquefier_* ...), so fasthydro.browse.PairBrowser, the wake notebook and wake_pyvista.py read the file unchanged.

With store_evolution=False no file is written at all: both legs are still read, resampled and hashed exactly as above (a reused background once), so last_event_diag, last_bg_key and the event count are what a full run gives, for a jetscape.particlize_h5.ParticlizeH5Writer that is then the job's only output (run_prod_jet.py --particlize-only). source/ and shower/ are not kept either. read_jet=False on top skips the jet leg's evolution altogether (nothing downstream of a particlize file uses it): its frame count and times then come from MUSIC's grid metadata (ntau_jet_music, MUSIC's own steps, instead of ntau_jet on the output grid), and frames_identical with the two checks built on it (same initial condition, droplets applied) is gone, as are the jet leg's jet_edge_e_max, jet_edge_e_max_eta and jet_hit_edge (n_hit_edge["jet"] is None). The background is still read once per run: its hash recognises a reused one. MUSIC_2 then does not store its evolution at all (set_store_evolution(False), music4gpu): its frame count and grid stay in its metadata.

Usage (see example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_prod_jet.py) 
jetscape = js.JetScapePerEvent(); ...; jetscape.Init()
writer = PairH5Writer("pair.h5", grid_mode="grid", out_grid=grid)
writer.attach(jetscape)                 # AFTER Init(): sets dump_hydro_only on MUSIC_2
jetscape.ExecInit()
for i in range(n):
    jetscape.ExecPerEvent()
    idx = writer.Exec()                 # both evolutions are live here
    jetscape.ClearPerEvent()
writer.Finish()

The writer is not a framework task: it has to be attached after Init() and called between ExecPerEvent() and ClearPerEvent(), the same pattern run_prod.py uses for H5BulkWriter. It needs no compiled extension itself, so it is testable with stubs.

docs.title: PairH5Writer(out_file_name='pair_evo.h5', *, bg_id='MUSIC_1', jet_id='MUSIC_2', grid_mode='grid', out_grid=None, tau_stride=1, choose_ntau=0, compression=DEFAULT_COMPRESSION, keep_bits=None, store_droplets=True, store_showers=True, keep_surface=(), provenance=None, extra_attrs=None, force=True, verbose=False, bg_layout='auto', reuse=1, store_evolution=True, read_jet=True, edge_e_threshold=None, verify_bg_reuse=False, extra_hard=False)
docs.text:
Write the background and jet legs of a two-stage MUSIC run as one pair file.

Parameters:

  • out_file_name (str, default: 'pair_evo.h5' ) –

    Output path.

  • bg_id (str, default: 'MUSIC_1' ) –

    Module ids of the two MUSIC instances (<name> in the XML).

  • jet_id (str, default: 'MUSIC_1' ) –

    Module ids of the two MUSIC instances (<name> in the XML).

  • grid_mode (('grid', 'native'), default: "grid" ) –

    grid resamples both legs onto out_grid; native writes MUSIC's own grid.

  • out_grid (mapping or Grid, default: None ) –

    grid mode only; as for jetscape.fast_h5_bulk.H5BulkWriter.

  • tau_stride (int, default: 1 ) –

    Keep every Nth stored MUSIC step, on both legs.

  • choose_ntau (int, default: 0 ) –

    0 grows the tau axis to the longest leg of any event; N > 0 pins it (longer legs are clipped, with a warning and a count at Finish()).

  • compression ((str, mapping or None), default: DEFAULT ) –

    jetscape.h5_compression spec for arr and arr_bg (default "blosc-zstd"; "lzf" is the old default). See README_h5_optim.md.

  • keep_bits (int or None, default: None ) –

    Round both legs to this many float32 mantissa bits (lossy, relative error <= 2**-(keep_bits+1)); None (default) is bit-exact. Both legs are rounded the same way, so arr - arr_bg is exactly zero wherever the legs agree.

  • store_droplets (bool, default: True ) –

    Write source/droplets and shower/.

  • store_showers (bool, default: True ) –

    Write source/droplets and shower/.

  • keep_surface (iterable of {"jet", "bg"}, default: () ) –

    Legs whose freeze-out surface MUSIC hands to the framework (skip_surface off), e.g. for jetscape.particlize_h5.ParticlizeH5Writer. The legs not listed get skip_surface on (the default for both). MUSIC must also build the surface for a kept leg (<freeze_out_surface>1 for that instance).

  • provenance (mapping, default: None ) –

    Overrides for the provenance attributes (hard_vertex, eos_kind, transport_mode, source_mode ...).

  • extra_attrs (mapping, default: None ) –

    More root attributes, written verbatim (run provenance).

  • force (bool, default: True ) –

    Overwrite an existing file.

  • bg_layout (('auto', 'full', 'shared'), default: "auto" ) –

    How arr_bg is stored. full: one copy per event, as always. shared: each background once (arr_bg_store, arr_bg_rows), arr_bg a virtual dataset over it that reads the same. auto (default): shared if reuse

    1, else full, so files without reuse do not change.

  • reuse (int, default: 1 ) –

    Events per background (setReuseHydro), for bg_layout="auto". Which events share a background is still decided from the data (diag/bg_id), never from this number.

  • store_evolution (bool, default: True ) –

    False: write no file (no evolutions, droplets or showers) but run every per-event step and check, so Exec()'s index, last_event_diag and last_bg_key are unchanged -- the bookkeeping a particlize file needs without the pair file.

  • read_jet (bool, default: True ) –

    False (needs store_evolution=False): do not read the jet leg's evolution; see the module docstring for what diag then holds instead.

  • edge_e_threshold (float, default: None ) –

    Energy density [GeV/fm^3], normally MUSIC's freeze-out value e(T_fo). Every event records per leg the largest energy density on the transverse faces of the OUTPUT grid (the first and last x and y planes, over all stored frames) as diag/{bg,jet}_edge_e_max, and on the eta faces as ..._edge_e_max_eta. With a threshold, diag/{bg,jet}_hit_edge is 1 when the transverse value exceeds it: fluid above freeze-out reached the edge of the stored box, so the stored evolution misses part of it (MUSIC's own, larger grid does not). None: the maxima only, no flag.

  • verify_bg_reuse (bool, default: False ) –

    A reused background is recognised by a fingerprint of its raw frames (grid, frame count and three whole frames), and then neither read nor resampled again: its frame hashes and edge maxima come from the event that first used it. Not with bg_layout="full" and a file, which stores the background in every row. True: read and resample it anyway and raise if the fingerprint matched a different background (a check for tests, at the old cost).

  • extra_hard (bool, default: False ) –

    The events have other hard scatterings (PythiaGun's ): store each event's scatterings/ (Exec's scatterings, SCATTER_COLUMNS rows).

docs.text: The liquefier's tau_delay [fm/c] (no droplet deposits earlier), or None without a liquefier. Valid after attach().

docs.title: bg_layout
docs.text: "full" (one arr_bg row per event) or "shared" (each background once).

docs.text: True if the jet leg has the liquefier, False in the null test, None before attach.

docs.title: attach(jetscape=None, *, bg=None, jet=None, liquefier=None, manager=None)
docs.text:
Find the two legs, the liquefier and the shower manager; set per-leg flags.

Call after JetScape.Init() (which reads the XML flags this overrides) and before the first event. Anything not passed is looked up: the legs by module id in jetscape.GetTaskList(), the liquefier on the jet leg (or, with the jet leg's <AddLiquefier> off, on the energy-loss manager's template), the manager through the signal manager.

docs.title: Exec(*, scatterings=None, **diag)
docs.text:
Write the current event's pair. Returns its index in the file, or None.

Extra keyword arguments are stored under diag/ for this event; with extra_hard, scatterings are the event's hard scatterings (S, 8). Must run between ExecPerEvent() and ClearPerEvent().

docs.title: write_diag(i, **scalars)
docs.text: Add per-event scalars after Exec() (e.g. the driver's wall time).

docs.title: Finish()
docs.text: Close the file. Idempotent.

docs.text: The shower/ group attributes FastHydro's PairedH5Writer writes.

docs.title: jetscape.surface_replay
docs.text:
python/jetscape/surface_replay.py

SurfaceReplay -- a FluidDynamics that hands a stored freeze-out surface to the framework, so iSS samples it exactly as it would have sampled the live hydro's.

replay = SurfaceReplay()
iss = create_module("iSS")
jetscape = JetScapePerEvent(); jetscape.Add(replay); jetscape.Add(iss); jetscape.Init()
jetscape.ExecInit()
for cells in surfaces:                       # (N, 32) float32, SURFACE_CELL_COLUMNS
    replay.load(cells)
    jetscape.ExecPerEvent()                  # iSS: GetHydroHyperSurface -> these cells
    hadrons = soft_hadrons_numpy(iss)
    jetscape.ClearPerEvent()

There is no initial state, pre-equilibrium or evolution: Init is overridden so FluidDynamics::Init does not insist on them, and bulk_info stays empty. The cells go in through FluidDynamics::StoreSurfaceCell -- the same call MUSIC's wrapper makes -- so iSS takes its normal GetHydroHyperSurface path.

docs.title: SurfaceReplay(module_id='SurfaceReplay')
docs.text:
Bases: FluidDynamics

Replay one stored surface per event (call load before each event).

docs.title: load(cells)
docs.text: The surface for the next event: (N, 32) float32, columns SURFACE_CELL_COLUMNS.

docs.title: jetscape.liquefier_io
docs.text:
python/jetscape/liquefier_io.py

Read the droplets and the kernel parameters out of a live C++ CausalLiquefier.

The droplets are what the jet deposited into the medium this event: one row per droplet, (tau, x, y, eta, E, px, py, pz) -- Milne position, Cartesian momentum in GeV -- exactly as LiquefierBase::add_hydro_sources stores them (LiquefierBase.cc:200-225). No conversion is applied. A MUSIC jet leg evaluates the same droplets itself, through HydroSourceJETSCAPE; these helpers only record them.

Nothing here imports fast_data or torch, so any writer can use it. FastHydro's liquefier_bridge wraps the same calls into its own types.

docs.title: droplets(liq)
docs.text:
The liquefier's current droplet list as an (M, 8) float64 array.

liq is a bound LiquefierBase/CausalLiquefier (droplets_numpy()). The list holds this event's droplets until a hydro with the liquefier attached clears it in its ClearTask.

docs.title: droplet_fluid(liq)
docs.text: Per droplet, the background fluid where it was made, (M, 4) = (vx, vy, vz, e): lab Cartesian velocity and energy density [GeV/fm^3] (e < 0: not looked up), or None for an X-SCAPE build whose droplets do not carry it (XSCAPE_DROPLET_FLUID). <CausalLiquefier><frame>fluid</frame> diffuses each droplet in this fluid's rest frame.

docs.title: liquefier_frame(liq)
docs.text: The frame of the causal diffusion: "bjorken", "lab" or "fluid". A build with only the two-frame option says it through bjorken_frame; one without either is "lab".

docs.title: droplet_fluxes(liq)
docs.text:
Per droplet, the sum of its point-sampled kernel on the hydro grid (X-SCAPE LiquefierBase::get_droplet_flux), or None if this X-SCAPE build does not normalize.

-1 marks a droplet that was never normalized. With normalize_on_hydro_grid true, the hydro receives each normalized droplet's four-momentum exactly; without it, flux times it.

docs.title: normalize_on_hydro_grid(liq)
docs.text: <Liquefier><normalize_on_hydro_grid> of this liquefier, or None for an X-SCAPE build without the normalization (every droplet deposits what its sampled kernel sums to).

docs.title: liquefier_params(liq)
docs.text:
The causal-diffusion kernel parameters as a dict of floats, keyed by PARAM_KEYS.

liq.params() gives the five input parameters. The two derived ones come from the object when it exposes them (CausalLiquefier.c_diff/gamma_relax), otherwise from the C++ formulas c_diff = sqrt(d_diff/time_relax) and gamma_relax = 0.5/time_relax (CausalLiquefier.cc:41-42).

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Look-up pages. They are not meant to be read in order:

  • Contribs and repositories: the four contribs, the repositories and images that make up a working setup, and the versions that belong together.
  • Tools: the command-line tools in utils/ for planning, monitoring, inspecting and moving productions.
  • AI assistants: using Claude Code, other coding agents and chat assistants with js-contrib: the instruction file in the examples, llms.txt.
  • X-SCAPE changes since 2.1: the physics and technical bug fixes and the new features of X-SCAPE contrib relative to the 2.1 release, third-party packages included.
  • Building this site: how to preview and change these pages.

The design notes, benchmark reports and production-readiness summaries that the pages refer to live in the repository's docs/ folder.

docs.title: AI assistants
docs.text:
An AI assistant can run a test event for you, write an analysis script against the readers, read a job log, or explain what is in a file. It does this well only if it knows how js-contrib is set up. Two things give it that knowledge:

  • an instruction file in your examples directory, AGENTS.md (with a CLAUDE.md that imports it), for assistants that work in your terminal and on your files: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and others;
  • this website as plain Markdown, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, for any assistant that can read a web page or a file: claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini and others.

docs.title: Coding agents: work in your examples directory
docs.text:
xscape-examples copies the examples and production scripts into a directory of yours (Your first event). That copy holds the two instruction files. Start the assistant there:

xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples      # once; in the container: xscape-examples /work/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples
claude                                 # Claude Code; or codex, cursor-agent, ...

Then ask in plain words, for example:

  • "Run one O+O event and plot the charged-hadron pT spectrum."
  • "Run two Au+Au jet events with seed 1, hadronize them with 200 oversamples, and check the logs."
  • "What is in out/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001_particlize.h5?"
  • "Write a script that reads this campaign and makes the wake in Δφ, with errors."

The instruction file tells the assistant how commands run in your installation (inside the container with docker run or apptainer exec, in the wheel's environment on a Mac, or in a source build), what a first test is, where the drivers and their options are, what the output files hold and how to read them, and the rules: test with one or two events first, start no campaign without your go, never write into the installation, do not treat oversamples as events, look options up instead of guessing.

assistant file it reads Claude Code CLAUDE.md, which imports AGENTS.md OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and most other coding agents AGENTS.md Gemini CLI GEMINI.md by default: set AGENTS.md as its context file in the settings, or tell it to read AGENTS.md any other tell it: "read AGENTS.md first"

CLAUDE.md is Claude Code's own file name; other assistants do not look for it. AGENTS.md is the name most tools share, which is why the text lives there and CLAUDE.md only points to it. Change AGENTS.md if you want to add rules of your own (your cluster's batch system, where your data are).

If your copy has no AGENTS.md

The files ship with the examples from 2026-11-12 on (later images and wheels). For an older installation, download them into your copy:

cd ~/xscape/examples
B=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example
curl -LO $B/AGENTS.md -LO $B/CLAUDE.md

With the container the assistant runs on the host and X-SCAPE in the image, so it wraps every command in docker run or apptainer exec; the instruction file shows how. Tell it your image (jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126, or the .sif file) and which host directory is /work. In a source checkout the files are in contribs/PyJetscape/example, and work the same way when the assistant is started there.

docs.title: Chat assistants: give them llms.txt
docs.text:
An assistant without access to your files can still answer from the documentation. llms.txt is the index of this site for language models (llmstxt.org): a short description and one line per page, each linking to that page as Markdown.

  • With web access (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini): put the address in your question. "Using https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/llms.txt, how do I run the O+O production on a SLURM cluster with Apptainer?" The assistant reads the index and then the pages it needs.
  • A single page as Markdown: add index.md to its address, e.g. https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md. This is smaller and cleaner than the HTML page.
  • The whole site in one file: llms-full.txt, 1.2 MB, roughly 300 000 tokens. That is more than most chat models take in one conversation. Use it where the assistant searches an uploaded file instead of reading all of it (a Claude project, a custom GPT, NotebookLM), or with a model that has a context of a million tokens.
  • For commands, also paste AGENTS.md: it is short and holds the rules and the per-installation command forms.

docs.title: What to check yourself
docs.text:
• Physics numbers. The analysis scripts are examples, not vetted results (Analyse). Ask the assistant for the cuts, the number of events and the error it used, and check a result against a second method before you rely on it.
  • Options and names. Assistants invent plausible options, XML tags and dataset names. The truth is --help, the folder's README.md, and h5_inspect.py for a file.
  • What actually ran. Ask for the exact command and the log lines that show the result. A line No CUDA device found means the run was on the CPU, which is slow and not the same numbers.
  • Cost. A campaign takes hours of GPU time and many GB of disk. Decide that yourself; the instruction file tells the assistant to ask first.

How the two llms files are made: Building this site.

docs.title: X-SCAPE changes since 2.1
docs.text:
The same table is in the X-SCAPE repository as RELEASE_NOTES.md.

Changes on the contrib branch (ef19d7f7, 2026-11-12) relative to the X-SCAPE 2.1 release (tag v2.1, 2026-03-05). The third-party packages X-SCAPE fetches (iSS, 3dMCGlauber, MUSIC, trento, the LBT tables) are included. MUSIC4GPU's own changes are not listed here; see jhputschke/MUSIC4GPU.

Fixes to code that was added after 2.1 are folded into the feature that added it.

  • Physics bug fixes: change the physics output of existing setups.
  • Technical bug fixes: crashes, hangs, memory, build and log noise. The output is unchanged.
  • Enhancements and new features: new or opt-in. Unless a row says otherwise, the defaults reproduce 2.1.

docs.title: Physics bug fixes
docs.text: Component Fix Effect in 2.1 PR / commit Liquefier A free-streaming parton that the liquefier absorbs is marked as absorbed (status -11). Before, it kept status 0/1. The parton was deposited in the medium and hadronized too. In two test jobs this double-counted 3% and 13% of the initial energy (issue #156). #154 Liquefier Each droplet is normalized on MUSIC's grid. Droplets at the hard vertex are deposited. MUSIC received 0.004 to 6 times a droplet's 4-momentum. 40% of 0-10% Au+Au events were off by more than 20%. Vertex droplets got eta = 0/0 = NaN and were never deposited. On by default; <normalize_on_hydro_grid>0 restores the old source. #155 CausalLiquefier The causal diffusion is solved in the frame of the Bjorken flow at the droplet's eta_s (<frame>bjorken, the new default), not in the lab's Cartesian frame. Away from midrapidity the deposit landed closer to midrapidity than the droplet (by about 0.4 units at |eta_s| = 1 and up to 0.9 units forward) and in a fraction of a cell. MUSIC reverted such cells, so deposited energy was lost: one test event kept 25% of it at tau = 2 fm/c. In Pb+Pb Z+jet the midrapidity wake came out 19% too large. Behaviour change: <frame>lab restores the old deposit; the two agree only at eta_s = 0. #189 Liquefier / MUSIC wrapper The jet source's hydro dtau is set for every initial condition, not only without a pre-equilibrium module. With string or pre-equilibrium initial conditions the droplet source was evaluated about 2.6 times too often. The hadronic liquefier's dtau stayed -1, so every droplet was deposited at every step. #146 Energy loss / MUSIC wrapper FluidDynamics::hydro_tau_0 and hydro_tau_max are initialized. MUSIC sets the energy-loss start time to its tau0, also when pre-equilibrium is kept in memory. Matter, LBT and AdS/CFT read the start time as 0 in practice, so <tStart> had no effect. Behaviour change: medium-modified energy loss now starts at the hydro tau0. #174 Matter No qhat table lookup at a negative index (ISR partons start at t < 0). Garbage qhat values, results that changed between runs with the same seed, and segfaults (O+O with ISR). 8c975d37 (#171) Colour tags (Matter, iMATTER) Colour tags come from one counter per event. Matter's tags overlapped between showers: 85% of O+O events and 67-83% of pp Z+jet events had a tag used twice. Pythia joined colour lines across showers without a warning. Affects colour-aware hadronization only (iColored, Colored); kinematics are unchanged. #181 iColoredHadronization Holes and liquefier partons are no longer handed to Pythia as ordinary partons. The tag-pairing loop no longer reads past the end of its vector. pythia.next() is checked. A failed fragmentation wrote the input partons out as hadrons. Now the event throws. ad1095be (#182) MUSIC wrapper MUSIC's reRunHydro flag is reset for every event, with a warning when the grid edge is hit. After one event touched the transverse grid edge, every later event of that MUSIC instance stopped at its first freeze-out check, silently. ca8dd84a (#141) MUSIC wrapper EOS_to_use is written before MUSIC is constructed. The first MUSIC instance in a process ran with whatever EOS the input file still held. a1753327 SurfaceFinder The flow is built as u = gamma (1, v). Lattice cells are counted with floor(L/d + 1e-4). u.u was 1 - v^4 (13% short at v = 0.7). The last cell in tau, x, y and eta was dropped: on a 4x4x2 grid the surface covered 26 of 32 fm^2. HybridHadronization uses only ratios of u, so u did not change its output. 88099402 MUSIC (CPU) Bulk Pi in the eta-direction flux: W_eta_p / W_eta_m take Pi_p / Pi_m (they were swapped). Wrong bulk-viscous contribution to the eta flux. MUSIC 9a304fb (#138) MUSIC (CPU) Charge source terms (turn_on_QS) use the coordinate factor instead of tau. CoorType can be set from X-SCAPE. Wrong charge sources in Cartesian mode; Cartesian mode could not be selected from X-SCAPE. MUSIC 3bc760d (#138)

docs.title: Technical bug fixes
docs.text: Component Fix Effect in 2.1 PR / commit 3dMCGlauber The draws for the target's hard-quark position are capped. Pinned from the jhputschke/3dMCGlauber fork; upstream PR chunshen1987/3dMCGlauber#7 was merged on 2026-11-04. Endless loop in about 1 in 500-1300 O+O events with ISR (issue #169). 21a06787, 3dMCGlauber b99d680 EvolutionHistory get on an empty history returns a vacuum cell. std::out_of_range stopped the job, in about 5% of O+O events (events without a medium). be68bc85 (#165) iSS wrapper An event with a hydro but no freeze-out surface gives no hadrons and a warning. exit(1). b8487c42 (#164) iSS Decay channels and sampled-hadron vectors are freed. About 1,900 leaked blocks per event. iSS 98deaff (#171) iSS One hadron object is no longer leaked per sampled hadron (part of the yield speed-up). Memory grew with every sampled hadron. iSS 01f7cf9 (#149) MUSIC wrapper The old framework copy of the evolution is freed before a larger one is allocated. Peak memory of a 0-10% Au+Au jet job was 20 GiB; now 14 GiB. #160 PythiaIsrMUSIC The example adds the pre-equilibrium module it needs. iMATTER finds the PDFs via PYTHIA8DATA (conda). Crash in MUSIC's InitArena; iMATTER needed $PYTHIA8DIR. 5ae7d2a1 (#164) Matter No qhat lookup outside the forward light cone. About 500 "Third instance" warnings per O+O event. 5900ebd0 (#164) Liquefier The energy-momentum check warns only above 5% of the incoming energy. Warned at 1e-10 GeV: 19 warnings for 25 droplets in one Au+Au event. d679b204 (#142) Build (CMake) OpenMP is enabled per language. On macOS OPENMP_FOUND was false: the framework was built without OpenMP and SurfaceFinder and ThermPtnSampler ran on one thread. 3955cef6 Build (CMake) libiSS and lib3dMCGlb are linked with -Bsymbolic. iSS and MUSIC4GPU both export a different pretty_ostream. Built together (CUDA, PyJetscape), iSS aborted in malloc on its first allocation. f25ba028, 73996c07 Build ThermPtnSampler.h includes <unordered_map>. Did not compile with some compilers. 16a658e9 trento hdf5_utils.cxx fixed. Did not compile with newer compilers (Linux arm). 9980458c LBT tables get_lbtTab.sh runs with bash 3.2 and joins the parts in numerical order. Failed under macOS's /bin/bash (declare -A). #186 JetScapeWriter The destructor is defined out of line, so its type information is emitted once. dynamic_cast to a writer failed across the Python module boundary. 9b3641b5

docs.title: Event generation
docs.text: Component Change PR PythiaGun <pTHatBins>: several pTHat windows per run, each with its own Pythia, seed and cross section. #152 PythiaGun <partonYMax>: rapidity cut on the handed-over partons; the cross section is scaled by the acceptance. #153 PythiaGun Z+jet: <trigger>Z with lepton acceptance cuts, <minPartons>. Final-state leptons are handed over and pass through energy loss like photons. #173 PythiaGun <extraHard>: the event's other hard scatterings, each with its own stream; minimum-bias mode. #187 ISR <Hard><ISR> in the XML task list builds the PythiaIsrMUSIC chain. <JetHadronization><name>iColored. PythiaIsrGun gets <pTHatBins>. The subtracted hard momentum is reported, with a warning for Subtract_hard_momentum other than 1. #164 PythiaIsrGun <partonYMax> / <partonYMode>: rapidity cut on the two hard partons. #165 PGun <rapidity> and <phi> of the parton (both 0 as before); <points>: several (pT, y) points in one run, event i takes point i mod K. #189

docs.title: Energy loss and hadronization
docs.text: Component Change PR Matter, LBT, iColoredHadronization Colour flow: Matter's recoils and holes keep their colour flow, LBT partons carry colour tags, and iColoredHadronization closes colour lines that end in the medium (<colour_closure>, default reconnect). See README_ColourFlow.md. #182 Energy loss (Matter, LBT) <Eloss><nThreads>: the showers of an event run in parallel on OpenMP threads (N threads, or -1 for OMP_NUM_THREADS). Off by default (0, output unchanged). When on, every shower gets random streams and colour tags of its own and droplets are flushed in the serial order: the output does not depend on the thread count, but a seed gives other (equally valid) showers than with 0. Runs serially, with a warning, unless all energy-loss modules declare support (Matter, LBT), showers run per event and there is no hadronic medium; ISR stays serial. O+O with ISR at 4 threads: energy loss 18 to 6.2 s per 40 events, jobs 13% faster; no gain in Au+Au jet jobs. #191 Matter <tStart_at_point>: apply the start-time cut at the point where it is used (default off). #183, #184 LBT LBT_TABLES_PATH / XML: table location configurable. LBT_TABLE_CACHE: tables in one block, shared read-only between jobs. #130, #163 Hadronization Reproducible re-hadronization: SetNextRandomSeed / GetLastRandomSeed for iSS and Colorless, <reseed_per_event> for Colorless and iColored, and iColored's <store_input> / HadronizeInput. #148, #172 Liquefier Only droplets that can deposit in the current step are evaluated. When none can, MUSIC skips the jet source (output unchanged). #141, #144 Liquefier The jet source and CausalLiquefier follow MUSIC's late time step (<late_delta_tau>, <late_tau_switch>). #171 CausalLiquefier <frame>fluid: the diffusion in the rest frame of the background fluid where the droplet was made (the droplet stores that cell's velocity and energy density). Opt-in; a droplet without a usable fluid takes the Bjorken frame. #189

docs.title: Hydro (MUSIC)
docs.text: Component Change PR MUSIC wrapper <freeze_out_surface>: switch off the surface export, globally or per instance. #142 MUSIC wrapper <slim_bulk_info>: a 24-byte-per-cell framework copy for energy loss (peak memory 14.2 to 8.7 GiB in a 0-10% Au+Au jet job, output identical). #162 MUSIC wrapper The framework copy is sized once and filled in parallel. #143 MUSIC wrapper Two-stage runs (background, then a jet leg): set_store_evolution, set_checkpoint_tau / set_restart_from, per-instance XML and <restart_from> from runJetscape, <output_momentum_anisotropy_vs_etas>. The background's checkpoint is taken a deposit half width before the liquefier's tau_delay, so jet legs with a droplet from the hard vertex restart from it too (output unchanged). #166, #168, #180, #190 Liquefier / MUSIC wrapper The jet source of a hydro step is filled from each droplet's light cone instead of asking at every cell (LiquefierBase::get_source_on_grid; used by MUSIC4GPU, bit-identical): 12 to 1.1 ms per fill. With the checkpoint change a Pb+Pb Z+jet job (1 background, 6 jets) takes 118 instead of 146 s. #190 Soft particlization Particlization from stored evolutions (SurfaceFinder on the stored history). 88099402 MUSIC (CPU) Two source-term pointers; a flag for dynamic grid padding. Pin cfcc264 to cee9460. #138 MUSIC4GPU Optional GPU hydro build (get_music4gpu.sh, USE_CUDA / USE_METAL). MUSIC4GPU's own changes are not listed here. 51e58ce7

docs.title: Particlization (iSS)
docs.text:
iSS is now pinned from the fork jhputschke/iSS (sampling_omp 0be6daf, was chunshen1987/iSS XSCAPE d242555). The yield speed-up and the correlated sampling were merged upstream on 2026-11-04 (chunshen1987/iSS#4); the SMASH-ready hadrons and the threaded sampling are only in the fork.

Component Change PR iSS Speed-ups, hadrons bit-identical: yields once per (mu, T) and delta f coefficients once per cell, 8 species per pass over packed cell arrays, a tabulated momentum CDF. About 56 to 15 s per event. #149, #170, #171 iSS Correlated sampling: random numbers addressed by the cell (Philox), switched in the XML. #151 iSS Correlated sampling and the surface preparation run on OpenMP threads (OMP_NUM_THREADS), hadrons bit-identical at any thread count: 2.4 to 0.43 s per surface at 10 threads (1.1 million cells, 100 oversamples). Uncorrelated sampling stays on one thread. cbc992e2, iSS 0be6daf SoftParticlization Opt-in compact hadron output (iSS fills flat arrays); SetNumberOfSamples. #148, #150 iSS SMASH-ready hadrons: <decay_smash_list>, <keep_primaries>; SampleCells for hadrons-only jobs. #172

docs.title: Output, build and running
docs.text: Component Change PR Writers RootBulkWriter and FastRootBulkWriter (hydro evolution to ROOT, e.g. for FNO training). Built only when ROOT is found. #129, #131, #157, #158 js-contrib js-contrib built with X-SCAPE (get_js_contrib.sh, CMake), including the PyJetscape Python interface. docs.title: The contribs
docs.text:
js-contrib is organised like fastjet-contrib: each contrib lives in its own folder under contribs/ and is switched on separately.

Contrib What it is Build Extra dependencies Docs on this site PyJetscape pybind11 bindings (pyjetscape_core), the jetscape Python package with the Pythonic layer, Python modules, the PyFNOHydro trampoline, the production drivers and examples C++ (-DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON); already built in the container and the Mac wheel pybind11; h5py, hdf5plugin, pyyaml; PyTorch optional ([fno]) Python, Run FnoHydro Fourier-neural-operator hydrodynamics as a C++ module through LibTorch, plus the bulk ROOT I/O library C++ (-DUSE_JS_FNO_HYDRO=ON) libtorch (~2 GB), ROOT Live PyTorch FNO hydro FastHydro MC-Glauber initial state and a fast 3+1D Milne finite-volume hydro solver, with the MATTER + LBT → CausalLiquefier jet-deposition workflow and paired background/jet evolutions pure Python, reuses PyJetscape PyTorch, scipy, h5py, pyyaml FastHydro Visualization 3D PyVista rendering of the hydro evolution, resampled from Milne to Cartesian coordinates, with a jet parton-shower overlay pure Python, reuses PyJetscape pyvista, scipy, vtk, imageio (imageio-ffmpeg for .mp4) 3D visualization

FastHydro and Visualization have no CMake build of their own. They read the framework through the PyJetscape bindings and so need a current pyjetscape_core.
